what: Host half of the frozen GPU core on a two-socket Emerald Rapids Xeon host with an L40S (machine M): host-ISA builds, pinning of the calling thread, call cadence and keep-warm. Paired latency of the measurement harness build of the final core (src/core/) in one process; per-row aggregates as recorded by the study. A shared host: ratios hold, absolute times are indicative.

machine.timed_cpu: CPU 0, a primary hardware thread on the GPU NUMA node 0, SMT sibling (CPU 32) idle, unless a row says otherwise

build.core: the final core (6g, the sources of src/core/), measurement-harness builds
build.launch_plan: gpu_sm_budget=64 (the ada64 plan) except avx2-b0 and avx512-b0

method.exactness_gate: Before any timing each build was compared per shot with the default AVX-512 build and with the ldpc reference: correction, observables, status word and soft output (soft output on the first shots of each row), five problems x three presets (a03125c3, a05c11, ms30).
method.screen: Paired A/A screen: 3 processes x 2 create orders x {main run (candidate against avx512), A/A run (avx512 against itself)}, 20,000 shots per side per run (120,000 pooled per side), both handles in one process, interleaved shot by shot, on CPU 0; pooled nearest-rank p50 / p99 / p99.9; verdict = the separation rule (every main-run ratio of a create order beyond every A/A ratio of that order and the pooled ratio beyond the A/A band).
method.full: The same paired protocol with 4 processes (160,000 shots per side back to back); cadence rows insert a 10 ms host busy-wait before every call, with or without keep-warm every 500 us during the gap and once 25 us before the call; 4,000 shots per side pooled over two sessions.
method.pinning: The avx512 build A/A in one process under five pinning conditions; per session one discarded warm-up process, then 4 processes x both create orders x 20,000 shots per side (320,000 pooled); two rounds in opposite order, each round's ratios against its own idle-sibling row: between-session ratios, not a paired A/B.
method.keep_warm_paired: Both handles avx512, the same shots and the same gap; only one handle kept warm, so the ratio is the keep-warm effect (2,000 shots per side; 2 processes x 500 shots x 2 create orders).
method.keep_warm_back_to_back: No gap; the driver enqueues the keep-warm kernel after a random half of the pairs and each pair is grouped by the treatment of the pair before it.

re_measurement.what: An independent re-measurement of the main rows with the same command, corpus and pinned CPU (rebuilt libraries byte-identical in .text to the study's). Quote these where they differ.

avx2_screen_vs_avx512.reading: AVX2 is about 4-13 % slower on these two problems, more than the study's own range

keep_warm_paired_bb288_unif_p1e-3_r18_z_.reading: 500 us reproduces (2.5 % gain); the 250 us row gives 2.6 %, not the study's 3.4 %: no preferred period between 250 and 500 us

corrections_when_quoting: The AVX2 penalty of the study's screen (p50 1.0003-1.0698, p99 1.0137-1.0535) is smaller than the re-measurement (see re_measurement).
The 250 us keep-warm period's 3.4 % p50 gain at a 10 ms gap did not reproduce (2.6 %, no_difference).
A create-order effect exists on bb144 xyz: first/second-created p50 1.0117 with the first-created handle slower in 11 of 12 runs; on bb288 z none (8 of 16).
avx2-b0 and avx512-b0 use the default 142-block launch table (gpu_sm_budget=0), not the 64-block plan of the other five builds.
The study's keep-warm paragraph names "bb144 z" for the paired keep-warm rows; the rows are bb288_unif_p1e-3_r18_z.
